analysis.title: Connecting the Dots: Themes from European results, UK Budget, Advertising & privacy changes, US midterms plus key research
key_insights: Market focus remains on AI economics. Hyperscaler results this week produced divergent share price reactions despite continued growth in AI demand metrics.

Multi-industry results (59% of coverage reported): beats are dominated by datacenters and semis, but the market is not rewarding that growth given the AI sustainability debate. Daniela Costa recommends a barbell: electricals on one end (Legrand upgrade, better product positioning for datacenters) and high-ROIC non-AI names on the other (Rational, Knorr Bremse, Konecranes, Volvo, Geberit, De'Longhi, Epiroc).
Multi-industry order beats over recent quarters have not translated into sales beats, which GS reads as longer lead times.

European consumer: one-off issues drove lower guidance at Reckitt and Haleon, but there are broader signs of pressure on wallets and a softer consumer environment. COGS and pricing for next year are coming into focus as hedges roll off.
European banks: the focus is NII and the growth trajectory with rate sensitivity. In-line results and misses have not been taken well (e.g. NatWest).

LNG: Technip Energies results put the next award cycle in focus. GTT, with almost 100% market share in LNG containment systems and an asset-light licensing model, was upgraded to Buy by Michele Della Vigna after a 12% post-results sell-off that GS calls overdone (revenue timing). GS raised GTT order forecasts by 18%.

CVC: the AUM print and a roadshow confirmed institutional fundraising appetite remains strong (watch Fund X). Exit flexibility has improved, including sales to other sponsors and strategic buyers, with less reliance on IPO markets.

UK Budget broadly met expectations. Banks saw relief, gilts reacted slightly positively (positive for utilities), and departmental spending plans look tight, potentially setting up a challenging Spending Review next year.

UK bank surcharge: a 3pp increase, lower than expected and time-limited. GS estimates a 1%-2% headwind to 2027E net profit for Barclays and about 4% for NatWest and Lloyds. The cash ISA limit was maintained at £20k.
Apple's privacy changes affect advertisers, including Publicis (covered in the On the Road with GS podcast).

Watch next week: US midterms, a BOE meeting where James Moberly expects a 25bp hike, and about 120 covered European companies reporting, including Rheinmetall, BT Group, Scout24, IMCD and flatexDEGIRO.
Rating changes: GTT up to Buy, Norsk Hydro down to Neutral, Poste Italiane reinstated at Neutral, HelleniQ down to Neutral, Gjensidige down to Neutral.

Hyperscalers: Amazon AWS revenue was short of some investor expectations, but compute demand continues to outstrip supply with capacity largely sold out for the next 2 years (Eric Sheridan, Buy). Alphabet Q3'26 Search slowed against tough comparatives and compute constraints require elevated investment (Buy). Microsoft Copilot revenue growth accelerated QoQ, daily users up about 50% QoQ and credit-consuming customers up 75% (Buy).

Intel guidance was significantly below the Street, driven by a significantly weakening PC market (James Schneider, Neutral). SK Hynix beat on stronger DRAM, NAND and HBM pricing (Buy). Samsung had an in-line 3Q26 operating profit and GS expects a strong 4Q26E on AI server demand (Buy).
Meta announced an equity offering. GS cites early Muse success and core business momentum (Buy).
Adyen fell 13% after a FY26 downgrade and withdrawal of mid-term guidance. GS expects mid-single-digit cuts to FY26 consensus (Buy). Logitech fell 11% on near-term margin headwinds (Buy).

Energy: Shell had a 19% operating cash flow beat and raised its Q3 buyback to $5bn (Buy). TotalEnergies stepped up buybacks, GS stays Neutral on relative valuation. Repsol's FY26 buyback of €1.8bn implies a 10% shareholder return yield (Buy).
Gas: TTF was up 8% WoW at 95 EUR/MWh. The Dec26 contract, also at 95, implies a 73% market-perceived probability of a low-Mideast-LNG-supply winter, up from 51% the previous week (Samantha Dart).
Energy trade view: refined product prices are highly volatile and GS stays long 2027 EU summer gasoline to hedge further geopolitical escalation (Filippo Cuscito).
Macro: Jan Hatzius says global growth is 'remarkably unremarkable' with downside risks. The most immediate concern is energy, and the AI boom is passing peak impulse.

FOMC: rates unchanged, GS (David Mericle) continues to expect a second and final hike in December, with a third hike in March possible if inflation is higher than expected. ECB: rates unchanged after the Council debated a hike, GS forecasts one more hike in December with another in March possible.
Strategy (Guillaume Jaisson): the rising cost of debt is starting to affect margins and could affect investment, but GS does not expect a systemic credit event and 3Q so far remains supportive.
Telcos: press reports say SpaceX is in discussions for 80k US cell sites, a step toward entering as a fourth nationwide player. GS says spectrum sovereignty should leave Europe more insulated.
Gaming: OSB handle growth rose to about +7% YoY in 3Q from about +6% in 2Q, and FanDuel's handle growth appears slightly stronger than DraftKings and BetMGM.
EU M&A was historically strong in 3Q, up 21% YoY, with Europe 48% of global cross-border deals. High-frequency indicators point to some moderation.

market_movers.rationale: GTT (GTT.PA) upgraded to Buy. The 12% post-results sell-off is overdone (revenue timing), order forecasts rise 18%, and the company has near-100% LNG containment market share with a licensing model.
Norsk Hydro (NHY.OL) cut to Neutral on a more challenging 2027 earnings set-up, with more Middle East units easing regional tightness and new Indonesian supply.
Poste Italiane (PST.MI) reinstated at Neutral. The TIM acquisition offers cross-selling and synergy potential, but much of the upside is in valuation.
HelleniQ Energy (HEPr.AT) cut to Neutral after a strong run. The refining view stays positive but freight is a near-term headwind.
Gjensidige (GJFG.OL) cut to Neutral as pricing normalises, leaving limited room to beat high expectations.
AWS revenue was short of some investor expectations, but compute demand continues to outstrip supply with capacity largely sold out for 2 years. Eric Sheridan is more confident on the 12m framework.
Q3'26 Search slowed against tough revenue comparatives, and compute constraints require elevated investment.
Copilot revenue growth accelerated QoQ, daily users rose about 50% QoQ and customers on usage-based Copilot credits rose 75%. On the US Conviction List.
Equity offering announced. Recent earnings showed early Muse success, core business momentum and intent to keep scaling investment.
Samsung Electronics had an in-line 3Q26 operating profit with slightly weaker NAND profit. GS expects a strong 4Q26E on AI server demand. On the APAC Conviction List.
SK Hynix beat on stronger-than-expected DRAM, NAND and HBM pricing.
Guidance was significantly below the Street, driven mainly by a significantly weakening PC market.
Not applicable to ASML. See ASM International entry below.
ASM International (ASMI.AS): advanced logic momentum drives an FY27 upgrade, with an expanding 1.4nm opportunity.
Logitech (LOGN.S) fell 11% on near-term margin headwinds, but product innovation underpins demand in core segments.
Adyen (ADYEN.AS) fell 13%. Topline was modestly ahead, but FY26 guidance was downgraded and mid-term guidance withdrawn. GS expects mid-single-digit cuts to FY26 consensus. On the Conviction List.
Dassault Systemes (DAST.PA): modestly better topline, FY26 guidance raised for a recent acquisition.
Orange (ORAN.PA): 3Q beat and raise, likely to reassure on France and Spain improvements.
Informa (INF.L): +5.4% group underlying revenue growth (+6.5% excluding non-recurring data contracts), broadly in line with GSe 10M26.
KPN (KPN.AS): 3Q revenue beat and guidance unchanged, more needed to prove structural EBITDA growth.
Telenor (TEL.OL): 3Q small beat, guidance unchanged, Norway and Finland growth concerns remain.
Prysmian (PRY.MI): beat and raise to drive a mid-single-digit 2026 adjusted EPS consensus upgrade.
Wartsila (WRT1V.HE) fell 8% despite a strong order beat and 2027 consensus EPS likely up at least low-single-digit.
Knorr Bremse (KBX.DE): 3Q rail vehicle systems order miss, minor low-single-digit EPS downgrades likely.
Epiroc (EPIRa.ST): low-single-digit adjusted EBIT miss as original equipment sales delivery masks margin resilience.
Safran (SAF.PA) fell 10% on results. Aftermarket remains supportive, oil is the sentiment overhang, and GSe revenue forecasts are 2% above consensus in the medium term.
Airbus (AIR.PA): EBIT broadly in line, FY26 guidance unchanged.
Boeing faces continued challenges in returning to normalized financial performance and in being the OEM rather than in the supply chain.
Shell had a 19% operating cash flow beat, driving a buyback upgrade to $5bn in Q3.
TotalEnergies: strong refining and gas trading drove net debt reduction and higher quarterly buybacks, but GS stays Neutral on relative valuation.
Repsol (REP.MC): FY26 buyback of €1.8bn implies a 10% shareholder return yield.
TGS (TGS.OL): management pointed to improving exploration activity, fully booked vessels, tighter capacity and more supportive pricing into 2027. On the Conviction List.
Technip Energies (TE.PA): margin recovery underway, next award cycle in focus.
Neste (NESTE.HE): strong 3Q delivery, well positioned for tightening renewable diesel markets.
SIG Group (SIGNC.S): strong 3Q results and guidance upgrades, on track for 2026 targets.
Endesa (ELE.MC): fading buyback support, flattening revisions, a weak Q4 outlook from wind and hydro, and high hedging that limits commodity upside.
Fortum (FORTUM.HE): weak numbers but largely expected.
UPM (UPM.HE): EBITDA 23% below consensus, all divisions below consensus.
HSBC (HSBA.L): 4% below GSe and in line with consensus. Banking NII was slightly disappointing given higher rates and stronger loan growth, with deposit competition emerging. On the Conviction List.
BNP Paribas (BNPP.PA): strong Q3, revenues about 3% above, opex in line.
Standard Chartered (STAN.L): beat and raise on guidance, $20bn net new money inflow, usual Q4 seasonal moderation expected.
Deutsche Bank: above expectations across revenues, opex, earnings and capital. No clear upside to 2026 consensus but a more de-risked set-up into next year.
Santander (SAN.MC): headline beat, but softer Spain and Brazil trends and downside risk to consensus overshadow the print.
CVC (CVC.AS): 3Q AUM slightly ahead of consensus, continued institutional fundraising appetite and more confidence in the Fund X raise. On the Conviction List.
Lloyds (LLOY.L): EPS cut for 2027-29E on slightly lower NII estimates and a higher tax rate after the UK Budget.
BBVA (BBVA.MC) fell 3%. Earnings in line, with Turkey NII strength offsetting weak Spain. Limited consensus changes expected.
Vonovia (VNAn.DE): outlook lowered across FY26-28, FY27 guidance below consensus and FY28 objectives materially reduced.
Reckitt (RKT.L) fell 5%. Organic sales growth was +3.3% against 4.1% consensus, a miss from US Lysol (35% of sales) manufacturing constraints. GS says the investment case is intact.
Haleon (HLN.L) fell 15% after a guidance cut on China and Latam headwinds. It missed organic sales in 3 of the last 8 quarters. On the Conviction List.
Beiersdorf (BEIG.DE): organic sales -1.3% on continued NIVEA weakness, margin uncertainty to persist.
Heineken (HEIN.AS): strong volume-led Q3 growth, focus on the 2027 efficiency drive.
Magnum Ice Cream Co. (MICCT.AS): Q3 organic growth +9.6% and guidance raised to +5.5% from 3%-5%, but the new guide implies only +0.8% organic growth in Q4.
Adidas (ADSGn.DE): ongoing apparel momentum, but investors stay cautious until footwear growth inflects.
Puig (PUIGb.MC) CMD: credible strategy, conservative targets, compelling upside. On the Conviction List.
DSV (DSV.CO): positive move after 3Q suggests structural concerns were priced in. GS sees a case for the stock doubling. On the Conviction List.
Apple F4Q26 preview: iPhone 18 family and Duo to drive growth in F2027.
Siemens Energy (ENR1n.DE) CMD on 11 Nov: GSe about 11% ahead of Bloomberg consensus 2030 EBITA, with potential to return €30bn out to 2030. On the Conviction List.

sector_views.rationale: Barbell: electricals (datacenter-exposed product) plus high-ROIC, less AI-exposed names such as Rational, Knorr Bremse, Konecranes, Volvo, Geberit, De'Longhi and Epiroc.
Market focus is on NII and growth trajectory. In-line results and misses are being punished. UK banks got relief from a smaller-than-expected, time-limited surcharge increase.
Strong LNG outlook with the next award cycle in focus (Technip Energies, GTT).
Pressure on wallets and softer consumer backdrop, one-off guidance cuts at Reckitt and Haleon, COGS and pricing in focus as hedges roll off. Luxury exit rate better than July-August.
Budget was a neutral event with relief from regulatory risk concerns and a supportive gilt move.
A tax increase, if confirmed, would be a negative, with Terna and Snam most affected and Enel least.

earnings_insights: Amazon (reported this week): AWS revenue came in shy of some investor expectations. Capacity is largely sold out for the next 2 years.
Alphabet (reported Q3'26): Search business slowed against tough revenue comparatives. Compute constraints require elevated investment.
Microsoft (reported this week): Copilot revenue growth accelerated QoQ, daily users +~50% QoQ, usage-based Copilot credit customers +75%.
Intel (reported this week): guidance significantly below the Street on a weakening PC market.
SK Hynix (reported 3Q26): beat on stronger DRAM, NAND and HBM pricing. Samsung 3Q26 operating profit in line with slightly weaker NAND profit.
Adyen (reported): topline modestly ahead of expectations, FY26 guidance downgraded, mid-term guidance withdrawn. GS expects mid-single-digit cuts to FY26 consensus. Shares -13%.
Shell (reported Q3): 19% operating cash flow beat versus expectations, Q3 buyback raised to $5bn.
Reckitt (reported): organic sales growth +3.3% reported versus consensus 4.1%. Shares -5%.
Haleon (reported): guidance cut, shares -15%, missed organic sales in 3 of the last 8 quarters.
UPM (reported): EBITDA 23% below consensus, all divisions below consensus.
HSBC (reported): result 4% below GSe and in line with consensus, banking NII slightly disappointing.
BNP Paribas (reported Q3): revenues about 3% above expectations, opex in line.
Vonovia (pre-release): FY26-28 outlook lowered, FY27 guidance introduced below consensus.
Magnum Ice Cream (reported Q3): organic growth +9.6%, guidance raised to +5.5% organic growth from 3%-5%.
Informa preview: +5.4% group underlying revenue growth (+6.5% excluding non-recurring data contracts), broadly in line with GSe 10M26 forecasts.

Upcoming: Apple F4Q26 earnings (preview published), c.120 European covered companies report next week including Rheinmetall, BT Group, Scout24, IMCD and flatexDEGIRO. Siemens Energy CMD on 11 Nov, Solaria CMD on 19 Nov.

risk_factors: AI sustainability debate is limiting the market reward for datacenter and semi beats.
Energy is the most immediate global growth concern (Jan Hatzius).
Winter gas tightness if Middle East LNG supply is low, with TTF at 95 EUR/MWh.
Rising cost of debt is starting to affect margins and could affect investment, though GS does not expect a systemic credit event.
Pressure on European consumer wallets, and COGS and pricing risk as hedges roll off.

China competition and macro weakness for luxury and consumer names.
vol_and_positioning: Energy: refined product prices have shown significant volatility. GS stays long 2027 EU summer gasoline as a hedge against geopolitical escalation.
Luxury: the exit rate was better than July-August, which GS thinks bodes well for the holiday season.
geopolitical: US midterm elections next week, with Alec Phillips covering polls, outcomes and implications for macro and markets.
Middle East LNG supply risk to Europe this winter, reflected in TTF pricing.
Further geopolitical escalation risk cited as the reason to stay long 2027 EU summer gasoline.
Oil is cited as the sentiment overhang for Safran and aerospace.
SpaceX reportedly in discussions for 80k US cell sites, with spectrum sovereignty leaving Europe more insulated.
China competition concerns for European industrials, with the China Competition Tracker accelerating sharply in September.
